These signed 8-bit, 20 MS/s IQ fixtures are copied unchanged from the MIT-licensed
libcrafter commit recorded in `sources.json`. They were generated by that
project's Rust transmitter, independently of Airwolf's Python fixture generator.
They are generated signals, not radio recordings or sensitivity measurements.

The corpus covers long/short preambles, 1/2/5.5/11 Mb/s, carrier/clock/timing
impairments, channel echo, length-extension boundaries, alternate scrambler seeds,
corrupt checksums, unsupported PBCC and truncated inputs. The source manifest
contains exact IQ hashes and expected payloads. Airwolf retains bad-FCS packets
as failed candidates; the upstream `reject` expectation means no CRC-valid frame.

The receiver adapts algorithms from the same upstream project. These fixtures
are therefore a cross-implementation regression, not an independent oracle for
every receiver assumption. The separate Python generator implements the IEEE
802.11b-1999 serial, CRC, Barker and CCK equations without receiver helpers.
